content.thinking: Found it — the anchor enumeration in my `fab.replay` was mistakenly using modular arithmetic (since anchors start from boundary 0, phase-order enumeration is wrong). Let's fix it:

arguments.command:
cd /workspace/submission && python3 - << 'PYEOF'
src = open('fab.py').read()
old = """        abo = [[] for _ in range(R + 1)]
        for rec in self.f['anchors']:
            nd = int(rec[0]); st = int(rec[1]); en = int(rec[2])
            first = st if st >= 0 else 0
            t = first + ((-first) % P)
            while t <= R:
                abo[t].append(nd)
                t += P"""
new = """        abo = [[] for _ in range(R + 1)]
        for rec in self.f['anchors']:
            nd = int(rec[0]); st = int(rec[1]); en = int(rec[2])
            k = 0
            while True:
                base = k * P
                if base > R:
                    break
                lo = st if base + st > 0 else base  # service only at t >= 0
                t0 = max(base, base + st) if base > 0 else base + st
                t0 = base + st if base > 0 or st >= 0 else 0
                # ranges always satisfy 0 <= st < en <= P, so:
                t0 = base + st
                if base == 0:
                    t0 = st
                tend = min(base + en - 1, R)
                t = t0
                while t <= tend:
                    abo[t].append(nd)
                    t += 1
                k += 1"""
assert old in src
src = src.replace(old, new)
open('fab.py','w').write(src)
print('patched (clean rewrite next)')
